newsitem.title: USA: S&P revises C.R. Bard l-term ratings outlook.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises C.R. Bard l-term ratings outlook.

text.p: NEW YORK, July 7 - Standard & Poor's today has revised its long-term ratings outlook on C.R. Bard, Inc. (Bard) to stable from positive.
In addition, Standard & Poor's has assigned its triple-'B'-plus rating to Bard's $300 million unsecured bank credit facility.

At the same time, Standard & Poor's has affirmed the company's outstanding triple-'B'-plus corporate credit and senior debt ratings, preliminary triple-'B'-plus shelf debt rating, and 'A-2' commercial paper rating.

Bard's investment-grade ratings reflect the Murray Hill, N.J.-based medical device manufacturer's solid position in several business segments, as well as its strong cash flow and moderate use of debt to finance growth.
Bard holds important positions in the surgical, urological, and cardiovascular products markets, with a particular strength in catheters and access port products.
New product development is a key to success, as product offerings are subject to technological changes and often become commodity-like in nature over time.
The company's product breadth is becoming a greater competitive advantage, as customers are increasingly dealing with fewer vendors.

The September 1996 acquisition of IMPRA, Inc. greatly enhances Bard's position in the rapidly growing vascular graft segment. Continued acquisitions and mergers may be expected as Bard broadens its product portfolio and builds upon its technological expertise.
Further international penetration in general, and increased domestic penetration in angioplasty devices in particular, present significant opportunities.

The company's ongoing need for product innovation is growing even more important as competitive and pricing pressures intensify. Moreover, the global trend to reduce health care costs at all levels could limit pricing flexibility.
Importantly, pro forma funds flow to lease-adjusted debt is sound at around 35%, and cash flow coverage of interest is comfortable at 8 times.

The unsecured bank facility is rated triple-'B'-plus, the same as the company's corporate credit rating. Since the bank credit facility is unsecured, the bankers will fare the same as other senior creditors in the event of default.
Ample asset coverage currently may be expected to dwindle in the default scenario.

In response to its somewhat lackluster performance, Bard has realigned its operations into three global operating units, increased its spending on research and development, announced a program to further rationalize manufacturing, and reclassified several product lines as discontinued operations. Still,
the company's diverse product base generates a predictable stream of revenues and earnings.
